title: 101 West 14th Street
materials: [18-foot floor-to-ceiling glass panels](https://www.archpaper.com/2023/09/oda-101-west-14th-street/), [triple-paned windows](https://parametric-architecture.com/101-west-14th-streets-modern-facade-creates-a-light-and-airy-feel-with-fractal-geometry/), [powder-coated aluminum frames and sandwich panels](https://www.archpaper.com/2023/09/oda-101-west-14th-street/)
summary_en: 101 West 14th Street is a 13-story residential condominium in Manhattan designed by ODA, featuring a distinctive "fractal" facade composed of 18-foot floor-to-ceiling glass boxes. The design utilizes repetitive geometric patterns to create a sense of lightness and depth, resulting in unique double-height living spaces that maximize natural light. Located at the intersection of Chelsea and Greenwich Village, the building anchors the corner with its setbacks and cantilevers, providing residents with expansive urban views through high-performance triple-paned glass fabricated in Italy.
built_evidence: The article states that the condominium "has been recently finished" and "consists of 13 stories and offers a total of 44 homes."

title: Al Dar Headquarters / MZ Architects
materials: Steel, concrete, glass, Kingspan Insulated Panels
summary_en: The Al Dar Headquarters is a landmark circular skyscraper in Abu Dhabi, designed by MZ Architects and completed in 2010. Its innovative semi-spherical shape was inspired by the symbolism of the circle and the seafaring heritage of the region. The building features a distinctive curved glass skin and an external structural triangular diagrid. It was developed in line with the LEED rating system, utilizing sustainable and recyclable materials such as steel, concrete, and glass.
built_evidence: The project is listed as a "Built Project" and the text states "This construction was completed by keeping the environmental factors in mind."

title: Archermit’s Feixue Pavilion
location: Pear Blossom Village, Luzhou, Sichuan, China
architects: [Archermit](https://parametric-architecture.com/tag/archermit/) (Lead Architect: Pan Youcai, Design Director: Yang Zhe, Technical Director: Chen Renzhen)
materials: Waterproofed concrete (petal-shaped roof slabs), extensive glazing, slender railings, water-covered rooftops, and tactile handcrafted surfaces.
summary_en: Feixue Pavilion is a nature education center located on a sloped site in Sichuan's Pear Blossom Village. The architecture is defined by five independent, petal-inspired concrete roof slabs that create distinct functional zones and allow natural light to filter through the gaps. The rooftops are designed to hold a thin layer of water, creating a reflective surface that integrates the building with the surrounding pear trees and mountain landscape. The project serves as a cultural anchor for regional rural revitalization.
built_evidence: The project was completed in 2025 and is currently functioning as a rural revitalization hub.

title: Bernard Tschumi Architects’ Circular Philo Building at Institut Le Rosey
materials: Steel, concrete, glass, and stainless steel for the double-helix slides. ([Parametric Architecture](https://parametric-architecture.com/bernard-tschumi-architects-philo/), [Lindner Group](https://www.lindner-group.com/references-pdf/preview?locale=en&objectId=62473))
summary_en: The Philo building is a circular academic and innovation center at Institut Le Rosey, designed by Bernard Tschumi Architects. The structure features a diameter of approximately 75 meters and houses classrooms, laboratories, and a central atrium. A defining internal feature is a pair of stainless steel spiral slides in a double-helix configuration. The building's material palette of steel, concrete, and glass creates a contemporary dialogue with the nearby metallic Carnal Hall and the campus's traditional stone architecture. ([Parametric Architecture](https://parametric-architecture.com/bernard-tschumi-architects-philo/), [ArchDaily](https://www.archdaily.com/1040322/philo-science-and-innovation-center-institut-le-rosey-bernard-tschumi-architects))
built_evidence: The project was completed in 2025 and was operational for the start of the 2025 school year. ([ArchDaily](https://www.archdaily.com/1040322/philo-science-and-innovation-center-institut-le-rosey-bernard-tschumi-architects), [Lindner Group](https://www.lindner-group.com/references-pdf/preview?locale=en&objectId=62473))

title: Centre Pompidou-Metz / Shigeru Ban Architects
materials: Wood, Steel, Concrete, Alucobond (manufacturers), Roof Membrane (PTFE-coated glass fiber fabric)
summary_en: The Centre Pompidou-Metz is a museum of modern and contemporary art featuring a striking 11,330-square-meter design characterized by its massive hexagonal timber roof. Designed by Shigeru Ban and Jean de Gastines, the structure consists of three cantilevered gallery tubes that offer framed views of local landmarks, all sheltered under a translucent membrane. The building's parametric timber lattice, inspired by a traditional Chinese hat, creates a large-scale sheltered forum that seamlessly connects interior and exterior spaces.
built_evidence: The project is categorized under "Built Projects" on ArchDaily and has a specified completion year of 2010.

title: India’s First 3D Printed House by Tvasta Startup in Pune
location: Godrej Eden Estate, Maan Hinjewadi, Pune, India
materials: Specially designed concrete mixtures, recycled waste materials from construction and industrial sectors.
summary_en: India's first 3D-printed house is a 2,200-square-foot villa located in Pune, developed by Tvasta Construction in collaboration with Godrej Properties. Built in just four months (June–October 2024) using automated robotic 3D printing technology, the structure features uniquely textured walls designed to improve thermal insulation. The project emphasizes sustainability by utilizing specialized concrete mixtures and incorporating recycled industrial waste, significantly reducing construction time and material wastage compared to traditional methods.
built_evidence: The 3D printed villa spans around 2,200 square feet and was completed in just four months, from June to October 2024.

title: King’s Cross Station / John McAslan + Partners
materials: Steel (16 tree-like columns for the concourse structure), Glass (for the vaulted roof), Ceramic Tiles (AGROB BUCHTAL Loop), Brick (for the historic facade restoration).
summary_en: The redevelopment of King's Cross Station in London features the Western Concourse, Europe's largest single-span station structure. The project includes a 7,500sqm semi-circular vaulted concourse with a striking steel and glass roof that integrates the historic Western Range and Main Train Shed. The design creates a seamless dialogue between the original 19th-century architecture and contemporary parametric engineering, providing significant operational improvements and a new public heart for the station.
built_evidence: With this multi-phased development now complete... the transformation of King's Cross station by John McAslan + Partners (JMP) represents a compelling piece of placemaking for London.

title: LAX New Concourse Completed by Woods Bagot Using Modular Construction
location: [Los Angeles International Airport (LAX)](https://www.flylax.com/), Los Angeles, USA
materials: Nine modular segments constructed offsite using an Offsite Construction and Relocation (OCR) approach.
summary_en: The Midfield Satellite Concourse South (MSC South) is a 150,000-square-foot extension of the Tom Bradley International Terminal at LAX. Designed by Woods Bagot, the project utilized a transformative Offsite Construction and Relocation (OCR) method, where nine large modular segments were built offsite and later assembled at the airport to minimize disruption and accelerate the timeline. The architecture draws inspiration from Southern California's modernist Case Study Houses, featuring light-filled interiors and a residential-scale atmosphere designed to enhance passenger well-being.
built_evidence: The title states the project was "Completed" and the text confirms modules were "assembled on-site into a fully functional concourse."

title: MAXXI Museum / Zaha Hadid Architects
materials: Glass, Concrete, Acoustic Suspended Ceiling/Wall Lining (StoSilent Sto)
summary_en: The MAXXI Museum in Rome, designed by Zaha Hadid Architects, is a contemporary art and architecture museum characterized by its fluid spatiality and fragmented geometry. Completed in 2009, the project features a series of intersecting concrete volumes that create a complex network of interior and exterior spaces, moving away from the traditional concept of the museum as a "container" and instead acting as a "campus" for art. The design emphasizes natural light, achieved through thin concrete beams on the ceiling combined with a glass roof, and integrates into the urban fabric of the Flaminio neighborhood.
built_evidence: Completed in 2009 in Rome, Italy.

title: One Central Park / Ateliers Jean Nouvel + Patrick Blanc
materials: Steel, concrete, glass, vertical gardens (hydroponic green walls), motorized mirrors (heliostat).
summary_en: One Central Park is a dual-tower residential and retail complex featuring the world's tallest vertical garden and a massive cantilevered heliostat. The project integrates 250 species of Australian plants into its facade and uses motorized mirrors to direct sunlight to lower park areas, creating a lush, sustainable urban environment.
built_evidence: Completed in 2014 in Chippendale, Australia.

title: Pierres Vives / Zaha Hadid Architects
materials: Concrete, Glass, [Reynaers Aluminium Curtain Walls (ConceptWall 50)](https://www.archdaily.com/catalog/us/products/11877/curtain-walls-reynaers-aluminium)
summary_en: Pierres Vives is a landmark institutional building that integrates three separate government departments: the departmental archives, a public library, and a sports department. The design is based on a parametric 'tree of knowledge' concept, expressed through a fluid, longitudinal concrete form with dramatic cantilevers and branch-like glazing patterns that signify the internal flow of people and information.
built_evidence: The project is listed under "Built Projects" and has a completion year of 2012.

title: Qatar National Convention Centre / Arata Isozaki
materials: Steel, Concrete, Architectural Mesh (Haver & Boecker), Folding Operable Walls (Skyfold)
summary_en: The Qatar National Convention Centre (QNCC) in Doha, designed by Pritzker Prize-winning architect Arata Isozaki, is a landmark of parametric design characterized by its Sidra tree-inspired façade. These organic steel structures support a 250-meter-long roof canopy, symbolizing the traditional gathering place of scholars. Opened in 2011, the building was a pioneer in sustainability, being the first of its kind to target LEED Gold certification. It features 3,500 square meters of solar panels and a highly efficient climate control system, housing a 4,000-seat theatre, a 2,300-seat multi-purpose hall, and three main tiered auditoria within its complex volume.
built_evidence: Officially opened on 4 December 2011

title: Qingdao Science & Technology Museum
location: Hong Island, Jiaozhou Bay, Qingdao, China ([Parametric Architecture](https://parametric-architecture.com/qingdao-science-technology-museum/))
materials: Metal cladding, vertical fins, and integrated LED lighting systems. ([Parametric Architecture](https://parametric-architecture.com/qingdao-science-technology-museum/))
summary_en: The Qingdao Science & Technology Museum, designed by von Gerkan, Marg and Partners (gmp), is a 40,000-square-meter facility on Hong Island overlooking Jiaozhou Bay. Shaped as a compact cube resting on a podium, the museum features a public pathway through its ground floor and large openings in its metal-clad façade to frame coastal views. The building serves as a hub for marine research and public education, organizing exhibitions around the theme of water and marine science within a layered visitor experience. ([Parametric Architecture](https://parametric-architecture.com/qingdao-science-technology-museum/))
built_evidence: The museum's architecture is described as "completed" and it is shown in photographs by CreatAR Images. ([Parametric Architecture](https://parametric-architecture.com/qingdao-science-technology-museum/))

title: Rolex Learning Center / SANAA
materials: Reinforced concrete, glass, steel, timber
summary_en: The Rolex Learning Center at EPFL in Lausanne, designed by SANAA, is a pioneering university hub completed in 2010. Its most distinctive feature is its fluid, undulating topological form, where a continuous 20,000-square-meter floor plan rises and falls to create a landscape of hills, valleys, and plateaus. This open-plan approach eliminates traditional internal partitions, using gentle slopes and light-filled patios to define functional zones like the library, study spaces, and social areas. The structure is composed of reinforced concrete shells and a timber and steel roof, enclosed by a transparent glass facade that offers panoramic views of the campus and Lake Geneva.
built_evidence: About a month ago the Rolex Learning Center designed by SANAA opened its doors.

title: Shenzhen Science and Technology Museum / Zaha Hadid Architects
materials: Stainless-steel panels, glass
summary_en: The Shenzhen Science & Technology Museum, designed by Zaha Hadid Architects, is a 125,000-square-meter cultural landmark in Shenzhen's Guangming District. The building features a U-shaped plan with a central atrium and includes 35,000 square meters of exhibition halls. Its exterior is clad in a system of stainless-steel panels designed for solar protection, and the project targets the highest three-star rating of China's Green Building Evaluation Standard.
built_evidence: The museum "opens today" and is featured with professional photography and tagged under "Built Projects".

title: Striatus: A 3D Concrete Printed Masonry Bridge in Venice, Italy
architects: [Block Research Group (BRG)](https://block.arch.ethz.ch/brg/content/project/striatus-3d-concrete-printed-masonry-bridge-venice-italy-2021) at ETH Zurich, [Zaha Hadid Architects Computation and Design Group (ZHACODE)](https://www.zaha-hadid.com/), [incremental3D](https://www.incremental3d.eu/), [Holcim](https://www.holcim.com/)
materials: Unreinforced 3D-printed concrete using a two-component (2K) concrete ink; dry-assembled masonry blocks without mortar or steel reinforcement.
summary_en: Striatus is a first-of-its-kind 3D-printed concrete masonry bridge, developed by ETH Zurich's Block Research Group and Zaha Hadid Architects. The structure achieves stability through its compression-only geometry, utilizing 3D-printed blocks that are dry-assembled without the need for mortar or steel reinforcement. This design approach allows for a circular life cycle where the bridge can be easily dismantled and its materials recycled, demonstrating a sustainable alternative for complex architectural forms.
built_evidence: The structure was exhibited at the Giardini Della Marinaressa during the Venice Architecture Biennale.

title: Structural Cellulose Wall
materials: Cellulose–casein composite, textile-supported frameworks composed of woven panels and textile-sleeved tubular elements.
summary_en: The Structural Cellulose Wall is a research project exploring the robotic fabrication of bio-composite architectural systems. Developed at the University of Innsbruck, it utilizes a cellulose-casein composite sprayed onto a textile-supported framework. The process integrates digital point cloud acquisition and robotic path generation to create differentiated material densities and adaptive geometries, blurring the lines between structure, surface, and fabrication.
built_evidence: Developed at i.sd structure and design at the Faculty of Architecture Innsbruck, the project explores a fabrication method in which a cellulose–casein composite is robotically sprayed onto textile-supported frameworks.

title: Xuelei Fragrance Museum
architects: Shenzhen Huahui Design (Lead Architect: XIAO Cheng) [ArchDaily](https://www.archdaily.com/1037854/guangzhou-xuelei-fragrance-museum-shenzhen-huahui-design), [Parametric Architecture](https://parametric-architecture.com/largest-fragrance-museum-in-guangzhou/)
materials: Red brick cylinders, glass curtain walls, natural skylights in central atrium. [Parametric Architecture](https://parametric-architecture.com/largest-fragrance-museum-in-guangzhou/), [ArchDaily](https://www.archdaily.com/1037854/guangzhou-xuelei-fragrance-museum-shenzhen-huahui-design)
summary_en: The Xuelei Fragrance Museum in Guangzhou is the world's largest museum dedicated to perfume and olfactory culture, covering 9,500 square meters. Designed by Shenzhen Huahui Design, its exterior features eight red-brick cylindrical volumes that abstractly represent perfume distillation equipment. The six-level interior, designed by Leaping Creative, offers a multi-sensory journey through 18 thematic galleries, featuring a scenic central atrium, interactive AI-powered fragrance personalization, and 300+ scent discovery points. [Parametric Architecture](https://parametric-architecture.com/largest-fragrance-museum-in-guangzhou/), [ArchDaily](https://www.archdaily.com/1037854/guangzhou-xuelei-fragrance-museum-shenzhen-huahui-design)
built_evidence: Certified by Guinness World Records as the 'Largest Fragrance Museum' on November 27, 2025; opened to the public in July 2025. [ArchDaily](https://www.archdaily.com/1037854/guangzhou-xuelei-fragrance-museum-shenzhen-huahui-design), [Guinness World Records](https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/778815-largest-fragrance-museum)

title: CopenHill Energy Plant and Urban Recreation Center / BIG
materials: Kalwall® (specialty facades), Unidrain
summary_en: CopenHill is a 41,000m2 waste-to-energy plant in Copenhagen that doubles as a public recreation center. The building features an 85m tall facade made of stacked aluminum bricks that houses the world's tallest climbing wall, while its roof supports a 9,000m2 artificial ski slope and hiking trail. Internally, it processes 440,000 tons of waste annually to provide electricity and district heating for 150,000 homes.
built_evidence: opens as a new breed of waste-to-energy plant topped with a ski slope

title: UNS Completes Wasl Tower in Dubai Rising 302 Meters Above the City
materials: Terracotta ceramic facade fins with metallic glaze, regionally sourced granite, aluminum, post-tensioned slabs, hybrid concrete columns.
summary_en: Wasl Tower is a 302-meter-tall mixed-use skyscraper on Sheikh Zayed Road in Dubai, designed by UNStudio. The building is characterized by its "contrapposto" twisting geometry and a high-performance terracotta ceramic facade that provides passive shading. It functions as a vertical community containing a Mandarin Oriental hotel, residential units, offices, and public wellness spaces, all integrated with sustainable systems like district cooling and CO₂-controlled ventilation.
built_evidence: Wasl Tower has officially been completed in downtown Dubai.
